propositions.name: earth_undergone_successive_changes
propositions.statement: The present state of the earth and its inhabitants is the last stage of a long, uninterrupted series of changes.
propositions.quote: the present state of the earth, and the organisms now inhabiting it, are but the last stage of a long and uninterrupted series of changes which it has undergone

propositions.name: organic_life_gradually_altered
propositions.statement: Throughout geological changes the organic life of the earth has undergone a corresponding gradual but complete alteration.
propositions.quote: the organic life of the earth has undergone a corresponding alteration. This alteration also has been gradual, but complete

propositions.name: complete_species_turnover_per_period
propositions.statement: After a sufficient interval no species existing at the commencement of a period still exists.
propositions.quote: after a certain interval not a single species existing which had lived at the commencement of the period

propositions.name: renewal_of_forms_repeated
propositions.statement: Complete renewal of the forms of life has occurred several times in the earth's history.
propositions.quote: This complete renewal of the forms of life also appears to have occurred several times

propositions.name: gradual_extinction_and_creation
propositions.statement: The present organic world derives from earlier geological periods by a natural process of gradual extinction and creation of species.
propositions.quote: the present condition of the organic world is clearly derived by a natural process of gradual extinction and creation of species from that of the latest geological periods

propositions.name: large_groups_widespread
propositions.statement: Large groups such as classes and orders are spread over the whole earth while smaller groups are confined to limited portions.
propositions.quote: Large groups, such as classes and orders, are generally spread over the whole earth, while smaller ones, such as families and genera, are frequently confined to one portion

propositions.name: widespread_family_limited_genera
propositions.statement: In widely distributed families the genera are often limited in range and well-marked groups of species are peculiar to each district.
propositions.quote: In widely distributed families the genera are often limited in range; in widely distributed genera, well-marked groups of species are peculiar to each geographical district

propositions.name: affinity_sequence_is_geographical
propositions.statement: The most closely allied species tend to be found in the same or closely adjoining localities so affinity tracks geography.
propositions.quote: the most closely allied species are found in the same locality or in closely adjoing localities; and that therefore the natural sequence of the species by affinity is also geographical

propositions.name: similar_climates_representative_species
propositions.statement: Countries of similar climate but separated by barriers have families genera and species represented by closely allied peculiar ones.
propositions.quote: In countries of a similar climate, but separated by a wide sea of lofty mountains, the families, genera and species of the one are often represented by closely allied families, genera and species peculiar to the other

propositions.name: distribution_in_time_like_space
propositions.statement: The distribution of the organic world in time is very similar to its present distribution in space.
propositions.quote: The distribution of the organic world in time is very similar to its present distribution in space

propositions.name: cotemporal_taxa_more_allied
propositions.statement: Species and genera occurring in the same geological time are more closely allied than those separated in time.
propositions.quote: Species of one genus, or genera of one family occurring in the same geological time are more closely allied than those separated in time

propositions.name: no_species_appears_twice
propositions.statement: The life of a species or genus has not been interrupted and no group or species has come into existence twice.
propositions.quote: the life of a species or genus has not been interrupted. In other words, no group or species has come into existence twice

propositions.name: sarawak_law
propositions.statement: Every species has come into existence coincident in space and time with a pre-existing closely allied species.
propositions.quote: Every species has come into existence coincident both in space and time with a pre-existing closely allied species

propositions.name: affinities_reveal_creation_order
propositions.statement: The natural series of affinities represents the order in which species came into existence each with an immediate antitype.
propositions.quote: the natural series of affinities will also represent the order in which the several species came into existence, each one having had for its immediate antitype a closely allied species existing at the time of its origin

propositions.name: common_antitype_multiple_descendants
propositions.statement: Two or three distinct species may have shared a common antitype and each may itself become antitype to further species.
propositions.quote: It is evidently possible that two or three distinct species may have had a common antitype, and that each of these may again have become the antitypes from which other closely allied species were created

propositions.name: forked_line_of_affinities
propositions.statement: When multiple species are independently formed on a common antitype the series of affinities becomes a forked many-branched line.
propositions.quote: if two or more species have been independently formed on the plan of a common antitype, then the series of affinities will be compound, and can only be represented by a forked or many-branched line

propositions.name: branching_tree_of_creation
propositions.statement: A branching tree is the best mode of representing the natural arrangement of species and their successive creation.
propositions.quote: Returning to the analogy of a branching tree, as the best mode of representing the natural arrangement of species and their successive creation

propositions.name: isolation_yields_peculiar_taxa
propositions.statement: A country isolated long enough for many series of species to be created on pre-existing types will have peculiar taxa.
propositions.quote: A country having species, genera, and whole families peculiar to it, will be the necessary result of its having been isolated for a long period

propositions.name: galapagos_allied_to_south_america
propositions.statement: The Galapagos Islands contain groups of plants and animals peculiar to themselves yet most nearly allied to those of South America.
propositions.quote: the Galapagos Islands, which contain little groups of plants and animals peculiar to themselves, but most nearly allied to those of South America

propositions.name: islands_peopled_by_winds_currents
propositions.statement: Newly-formed islands are first peopled by the action of winds and currents at a period remote enough for original species to die out.
propositions.quote: They must have been first peopled, like other newly-formed islands, by the action of winds and currents, and at a period sufficiently remote to have had the original species die out

propositions.name: recent_islands_lack_peculiar_groups
propositions.statement: No geologically very recent island is known to possess generic or family groups or many species peculiar to itself.
propositions.quote: no example is known of an island which can be proved geologically to be of very recent origin (late in the Tertiary, for instance), and yet possesses generic or family groups, or even many species peculiar to itself

propositions.name: mountain_range_representative_species
propositions.statement: A long-elevated mountain range produces very different species and representative genera on its two sides.
propositions.quote: When a range of mountains has attained a great elevation, and has so remained during a long geological period, the species of the two sides at and near their bases will be often very different

propositions.name: malacca_borneo_early_continent
propositions.statement: The shallow sea between Malacca Java Sumatra and Borneo was probably a continent or large island at an early epoch.
propositions.quote: The shallow sea between the Peninsula of Malacca, Java, Sumatra and Borneo was probably a continent or large island at an early epoch

propositions.name: britain_recent_no_peculiar_species
propositions.statement: Britain shows recent geological separation from the continent and has scarcely a species peculiar to it.
propositions.quote: Our own island is an example of this, its separation from the continent being geologically very recent, and we have consequently scarcely a species which is peculiar to it

propositions.name: extinction_from_altered_conditions
propositions.statement: Gradual geological changes have occasionally modified external conditions enough to render certain species impossible.
propositions.quote: Geological changes, however gradual, must occasionally have modified external conditions to such an extent as to have rendered the existence of certain species impossible

propositions.name: general_progression_of_organization
propositions.statement: Mollusca and Radiata existed before Vertebrata and progression from Fishes to Reptiles to Mammalia and lower to higher mammals is indisputable.
propositions.quote: Mollusca and Radiata existed before Vertebrata, and the progression from Fishes to Reptiles and Mammalia, and also from the lower mammals to the higher, is indisputable

propositions.name: theory_is_gradual_change_not_progression
propositions.statement: The hypothesis though appearing progressive is in reality only a theory of gradual change.
propositions.quote: though it may appear to some readers essentially a theory of progression, it is in reality only one of gradual change

propositions.name: lower_forms_serve_as_antitypes
propositions.statement: When higher groups become extinct the lower forms that resisted altered conditions serve as antitypes on which new races are founded.
propositions.quote: whenever any of the higher groups have become nearly or quite extinct, the lower forms which have better resisted the modified physical conditions have served as the antitypes on which to found the new races

propositions.name: quiescence_favors_abundance
propositions.statement: A long period of quiescence or stability in physical conditions is most favourable to the greatest abundance of organic life.
propositions.quote: a long period of quiescence or stability in the physical conditions of a district would be most favourable to the existence of organic life in the greatest abundance

propositions.name: rapid_or_large_change_unfavorable
propositions.statement: A change in physical conditions if rapid or if gradual but to a great amount is highly unfavourable to individuals.
propositions.quote: a change in the physical conditions of a district, even small in amount, if rapid, or even gradual, if to a great amount, would be highly unfavourable to the existence of individuals

propositions.name: geological_activity_extinction_exceeds_creation
propositions.statement: In a period of geological activity extinctions may exceed creations so the number of species diminishes.
propositions.quote: In a period of geological activity, on the other hand, it, seems probable that the extinctions might exceed the creations, and the number of species consequently diminish

propositions.name: knowledge_of_past_life_fragmentary
propositions.statement: Our knowledge of the former inhabitants of the earth is necessarily most imperfect and fragmentary.
propositions.quote: our knowledge of the whole series of the former inhabitants of the earth is necessarily most imperfect and fragmentary

propositions.name: rudimentary_organs_have_no_function
propositions.statement: Rudimentary organs really exist and in most cases have no special function in the animal economy.
propositions.quote: these really do exist, and in most cases have no special function in the animal æconomy, is admitted by the first authorities in comparative anatomy

propositions.name: rudimentary_organ_examples
propositions.statement: Familiar rudimentary organs include hidden limbs in snake-like lizards anal hooks of the boa constrictor and finger-bones in Manatus and whale paddles.
propositions.quote: The minute limbs hidden beneath the skin in many of the snake-like lizards, the anal hooks of the boa constrictor, the complete series of jointed finger-bones in the paddle of the Manatus and whale

propositions.name: independent_creation_leaves_rudiments_unexplained
propositions.statement: If each species were created independently without relation to pre-existing species rudimentary organs would be inexplicable.
propositions.quote: If each species has been created independently, and without any necessary relations with pre-existing species, what do these rudiments, these apparent imperfections mean?

propositions.name: every_change_shall_be_gradual
propositions.statement: The great law regulating the peopling of the earth is that every change shall be gradual and no new creature widely differs from anything before existing.
propositions.quote: the great law which has regulated the peopling of the earth with animal and vegetable life is, that every change shall be gradual; that no new creature shall be formed widely differing from anything before existing

propositions.name: penguin_flapper_antitype_of_wing
propositions.statement: The scaly flapper of the penguin remains as an antitypal sketch of a wing adapted for flight.
propositions.quote: We still see remaining an antitypal sketch of a wing adapted for flight in the scaly flapper of the penguin

propositions.name: gaps_softened_by_intermediates
propositions.statement: The great gaps between fishes reptiles birds and mammals would be softened down by intermediate groups if all extinct forms were known.
propositions.quote: The great gaps that exist between fishes, reptiles, birds and mammals would then, no doubt, be softened down by intermediate groups

propositions.name: law_necessitates_facts
propositions.statement: The hypothesis is superior because it not merely explains but necessitates what exists.
propositions.quote: It also claims a superiority over previous hypotheses, on the ground that it not merely explains, but necessitates what exists

propositions.name: facts_alone_should_disprove
propositions.statement: The hypothesis should be disproved by facts alone and not by a-priori arguments against its probability.
propositions.quote: he expects facts alone to be brought to disprove it; not a à-priori arguments against its probabiliy
